findings.text: lint.identifiers.home adds a new error, findings.identifier-unhomed, so `lint` now exits 1 on trees it used to accept. baseline.run.lint and baseline.diff.since both require `lint` to exit 0, in the spec root and at a --since revision, so manifest, diff and pack now refuse with exit status 2 a tree, or a revision's tree, that holds an identifier whose first segment names no place. upkeep.rehome.lint was amended to tolerate exactly this error, but neither baseline rule is among the candidates and neither has an Examples row for the new case, for instance a `diff --since` naming a commit from before the tree was rehomed.

The home rule's Rationale says one mistake is reported once, but its guard spares only a capability identifier of several segments. A malformed identifier such as `Search.attempts`, or a system identified as `proviso`, now gets `findings.identifier-unhomed` beside `findings.identifier-malformed` or `findings.system-identifier`, and no Examples row shows whether that second error is meant.

`upkeep.rehome.given` and `upkeep.rehome.collision` both fire when `rehome` "has planned" its renames, and no rule says which comes first. Only the rows of `upkeep.rehome.given` ("planned, then refused as a collision"; "instead of `system.snapshot`, a term's identifier") imply that collisions are checked against the given identifiers rather than the derived ones. Nothing decides the exit status of a run where one `--rename` value cannot be taken (2) and another rename collides (1).

`upkeep.rehome.place` (Otherwise) and the widened `upkeep.rehome.lint` now give an identifier to elements whose identifier names no place, such as a contract's name alone, which never moved. Yet the Goal of `upkeep.rehome` still speaks only of identifiers that name "another place than its identifier home", and the Goal of `upkeep` and the system Scope only of "elements that moved".

A malformed identifier whose first segment differs from its place only in form, such as `Lint.run` in the capability `lint`, meets the Otherwise of both `lint.identifiers.form` and `lint.identifiers.home`, so one mistake gives two errors. The Rationale of `lint.identifiers.home` says "the one mistake is reported once" for a capability identifier of several segments, but no row or rule decides the malformed case.

An amendment that gives a capability another identifier, or removes one whose elements move elsewhere, leaves identifiers whose first segment names no capability (lint.identifiers.home's `checks.run` row). Lint then reports an error, so impact, judge and verify refuse the amendment by coherence.run.lint, and rehome refuses it by upkeep.rehome.baseline because the manifest does not record that tree. No rule says how such an amendment is checked and accepted. The cases in upkeep.rehome.place (`checks.run` renamed to `coherence.checks.run`) and the 'awkward' case in the upkeep.rehome Rationale assume a recorded tree that the workflow cannot produce, since manifest also refuses a tree with a lint error (baseline.run.lint).

The amendment widens the system Scope, the Upkeep Goal and the Rehoming Goal: `rehome` now also gives identifiers that name no place the identifiers of their place, and takes `--rename`. The install capability's Goal, the `proviso-rehome` row of `install.init.skills` and that skill's row in `installed_files` still say only that it 'gives moved elements the identifiers of their place'. So the description of the installed skill no longer matches the Scope it serves.

A tree with no manifest.sum that holds an identifier naming no place, such as a recovered tree before its first acceptance, is refused by `manifest` (lint error, baseline.run.lint) and by `rehome` (no manifest, upkeep.rehome.baseline). No rule or rationale says how such a tree reaches its first acceptance, yet the new row of baseline.run.lint says that `rehome` repairs it first.

Rehome needs a tree the manifest records (upkeep.rehome.baseline), but manifest refuses any tree with a lint error (baseline.run.lint), and lint.identifiers.home makes an unhomed identifier an error. So the only unhomed identifiers rehome can ever see come from trees accepted before this rule existed. An amendment that removes or re-identifies a capability while elements keep its first segment can never be accepted, and the cases in upkeep.rehome.place and upkeep.rehome.given of `checks.run` with no capability identified as `checks` any more, and the 'awkward' example in the upkeep.rehome Rationale, are cases rehome never reaches. That works against upkeep's Rationale that a move keeps its identifiers so that it is cheap.

The guard of upkeep.rehome.lint lets lint exit with 1 'for no other reason than identifiers whose first segment is neither "system" nor the identifier of a capability'. That description also fits a system identified as `proviso` (reported as findings.system-identifier) and a malformed identifier such as `Lint.run` (findings.identifier-malformed), both of which lint.identifiers.home deliberately keeps out of findings.identifier-unhomed. Read literally, rehome would run on such a tree and plan `proviso` → `system.proviso`. The guard also says 'the identifier of a capability' where lint.identifiers.home says 'the first segment of the identifier of a capability'.

lint.identifiers.home counts as a place only the first segment of the identifier of a capability of the spec tree. No rule says what that is for a capability folder without capability.md, or whose capability.md does not open with its element, or whose identifier is malformed. Read literally, every element of such a capability is also reported as identifier-unhomed, so one mistake (capability-file-missing, element-missing or identifier-malformed) is reported once per element, against the rule's own Rationale that one mistake is reported once.

The guard of upkeep.rehome.lint lets rehome run on a tree whose only errors are about "[identifiers] whose first segment is neither "system" nor the [identifier] of a capability". That is a paraphrase, not the finding `findings.identifier-unhomed`, and it covers cases lint.identifiers.home leaves to other findings: a malformed identifier such as `Lint.run` (`findings.identifier-malformed`) and a system identifier such as `proviso` (`findings.system-identifier`). A tree whose only errors are those would pass the guard, and upkeep.rehome.place would then plan `lint.Lint.run` or `system.proviso`.

An amendment that gives a capability another identifier, or removes a capability whose identifier still prefixes elements, makes those identifiers unhomed in the same amendment. Lint then stops diff, pack, impact, verify and manifest, and upkeep.rehome.baseline refuses rehome while the amendment is in progress, so no rule says how such an amendment goes on. The state that upkeep.rehome.place's `checks.run` row and upkeep.rehome's Rationale ("whose capability has since been given another identifier") describe can only come from a manifest written before lint.identifiers.home existed.

The constraint system.acceptance-tests still says that if a new identifier gives the test name of another identifier, "an amendment renames the element first". The amendment adds `--rename` precisely so that a taken or awkward identifier is given another one without an amendment, which upkeep.rehome's Rationale states. The constraint was not brought into line, so it now demands an amendment for a case the amended tree resolves without one.

The Goal of the capability `install` still says its skills "give moved elements the identifiers of their place". The amendment widened that purpose to elements that moved "or whose identifiers name no place" in the system's Scope, the Goal of `upkeep`, the rehome row of `installed_files` and the row for `.claude/skills/proviso-rehome/SKILL.md` in `install.init.skills`. So the capability describes the skill it installs more narrowly than its own rule and parameter do.
